scope: The late nineteenth-century Cathedral of Santo Domingo, with its stone north entrance, clock and bell stage, long Gothic nave, lower chapel roofs and the west front.

quallaFirst.observedFeatures: The printed photograph shows the same large north arched entrance and flanking small arches, clock stage and open bell stage, two stone roof tiers and the park ahead of the cathedral.
quallaFirst.excluded: The unattributed late-19th-century file lacks original provenance. The modern Creative Commons Attribution ShareAlike photographs were excluded. None were used as modeling references.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The Dominican ministry’s guide identifies the Gothic cathedral, the three naves and circular pillars and dates the sixteenth-century building.
Original geophysical and architectural survey of the basilica connects the widths and heights of the central and side naves.
The March 1915 United States periodical includes photographs of the north front and the preserved west façade. The individual west-front plate is a candidate for evidence binding.
Architectural restoration report documents the chapter house above the north Gothic gate, the public clock, its 1894 storm damage and the removal of the addition around 1916.
